context.person: A traveler whose booked flight was canceled before departure
context.surface: In-app disruption card shown when the traveler opens the affected trip
context.user_goal: Understand the replacement and choose whether to accept it, take another flight, or request a refund

product_state.preceding_state: The traveler booked Flight 207 for September 18, 2026, at 4:20 PM, selected seat 12A, and added one checked bag.
product_state.current_state: Flight 207 was canceled and the airline provisionally rebooked the traveler on Flight 418 for September 19, 2026, at 10:20 AM.
known_facts: The replacement is Flight 418 on September 19 at 10:20 AM.
Accepting the replacement adds no fare.
The checked bag transfers, but seat 12A does not.
The primary action accepts Flight 418 and opens seat selection.
The secondary action opens choices to take another available flight or request a refund.
Opening the other options does not accept or cancel Flight 418.
forbidden_claims: The traveler has already accepted Flight 418.
The replacement requires an additional fare.
Opening other options automatically cancels Flight 418.

current_content.headline: Good news!
current_content.body: We found you another flight. Continue to see your updated trip.

challenge: Rewrite the disruption card so the traveler understands that the original flight was canceled, the replacement flight and time, the fare and baggage effects, the missing seat assignment, and the available choices.

constraints.character_counting_rule: Count spaces, numbers, and punctuation as characters.

interaction_contract.primary_action: Accept Flight 418 and open seat selection.
interaction_contract.secondary_action: Open choices for another available flight or a refund without accepting or canceling Flight 418.
interaction_contract.consequence_to_preserve: Flight 207 is canceled; Flight 418 leaves September 19 at 10:20 AM at no extra fare, and the checked bag transfers but seat 12A does not.
interaction_contract.recovery_to_preserve: The traveler can accept Flight 418 and choose a seat, or open other options to choose another flight or request a refund.

rationale_requirements: Explain how the wording leads with the canceled state instead of the replacement.
Explain how the replacement time, fare, baggage, and seat effects remain visible.
Explain how both actions disclose their destinations and effects.
Report the character count for every candidate field.
Name unresolved operational questions instead of inventing deadlines or refund timing.
